correctness.rationale: The three cases are disjoint and exhaustive. With no label \(2\), the zero-defense rule forces the all-one labeling. With label \(2\) in exactly one part, that part may contain only labels \(1,2\), must contain a \(2\), and at least one outside vertex must carry label \(1\); these conditions are also sufficient. With label \(2\) in at least two parts, every zero sees a \(2\) in another part and every \(2\) has a positive neighbor in another part, so no additional restrictions remain. Multiplying the independent part contributions gives the stated polynomial; evaluating at \(z=1\) gives the count. The finite checker is corroborative only.
risks: The minimum-weight corollary is largely prior-implied and is not treated as the novelty basis.
